security_audit.summary: The skill contains legitimate motion-graphics tooling, but its map and localization helpers execute local programs, access remote resources, and handle an optional API credential. Review found unsafe autonomous update guidance, an unsandboxed browser with remote scripts, and missing output-path and external-content trust controls. Most template-literal, documentation, and visual-animation matches were false positives.

remediation.issue: The map baker launches Chrome with --no-sandbox while loading remote CDN scripts and map data.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --no-sandbox. Run the baker in a sandboxed container and vendor or integrity-verify all browser dependencies and map assets.

remediation.issue: NAME is environment-controlled and is joined into output file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only a safe basename character set and verify every resolved output path remains inside the selected output directory.

remediation.issue: The workflow requests a silent npx update before user confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, pin the package version, and verify package provenance before installing or updating.

remediation.issue: Fetched assets and search results can be passed into autonomous agent workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Treat all external content as data, strip instruction-like text, and require approval before executing actions derived from it.

remediation.issue: Optional automatic localization uploads image data and sends an API key in a query URL.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain consent before upload, use an Authorization header, and validate the returned coordinates before using them.

semantic_findings.title: Unsandboxed browser executes remote content
semantic_findings.description: The map baker disables the Chrome sandbox and loads JavaScript and map resources from remote endpoints. A compromised remote dependency or browser exploit could affect the host build environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly loads remote scripts and passes --no-sandbox to Puppeteer. These controls combine into a clear host-isolation risk.

semantic_findings.title: Output path traversal through environment name
semantic_findings.description: The map baker uses the unvalidated NAME environment value to form frame directories and output filenames. A value containing path separators can escape the intended output directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: NAME is directly concatenated into paths without basename validation or containment checks.

semantic_findings.title: Unattended remote package update
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to run a silent npx update before work begins, allowing remotely fetched package code to change the installed skill without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to update silently and describe global updates from GitHub.

semantic_findings.title: External content prompt injection exposure
semantic_findings.description: The autonomous workflow sources external assets and includes resolved asset information in subagent context without an explicit rule that fetched content is untrusted data. Malicious webpages or assets can contain instruction-like content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow is autonomous and forwards resolved external assets to subagents. The reviewed instructions do not establish a content trust boundary.

content.value_statement: Short motion graphics can be difficult to plan, build, and verify consistently. This skill guides a structured workflow for design-led videos, overlays, charts, maps, and branded animations.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests into motion graphic categories such as charts, maps, and logo reveals.
Creates a shot plan before composition work begins.
Builds short visual sequences from reusable composition patterns.
Renders MP4 video and supports WebM or MOV overlays when available.
Generates proof snapshots and checks output duration and file presence.
Supports asset-first workflows for user-provided images, logos, webpages, and articles.
limitations: It is intended for short design-led clips, usually under 30 seconds.
It does not provide narration, live-action footage, or multi-scene storytelling.
Map baking and optional localization require local tools and may access external services.
Output quality depends on available assets, fonts, rendering tools, and the selected project environment.

use_cases.title: Animate a product metric
use_cases.description: Turn a single KPI into a short count-up, ring, or chart animation for a launch update.

use_cases.title: Create a branded lower third
use_cases.description: Produce a reusable name, title, or callout overlay that matches supplied brand assets.

use_cases.title: Explain a geographic update
use_cases.description: Create a short map animation that highlights regions, connects locations, or zooms to a destination.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: animate a statistic
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five-second motion graphic that counts from 0 to 75 percent. Use a clean dark background and a clear final hold.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: build a logo reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-second logo reveal using my supplied logo. Use restrained motion, preserve clear space, and export an MP4.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: animate data
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an eight-second animated bar chart from these quarterly values: 42, 57, 68, and 81. Add a title and label each bar.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: map highlight
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ten-second map animation that zooms from Europe to Paris and highlights Paris with our blue brand color. Include a final location label.

output_examples.input: Create a five-second animated statistic for 75 percent adoption.
output: A short count-up animation from 0 to 75 percent.
A final hold with the metric and a concise label.
A rendered video file and proof snapshots.

output_examples.input: Create a branded lower third for Maya Chen, Product Director.
output: A reusable lower-third composition using the supplied brand colors.
An entrance, readable hold, and exit animation.
A rendered overlay-ready video when the requested format is available.

best_practices: Provide the target duration, aspect ratio, brand assets, and final message before building.
Use licensed, user-provided, or approved assets for logos, images, webpages, and articles.
Review proof snapshots and rendered output before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for long narrated videos or multi-scene stories.
Do not request unsupported facts or use unverified news content as final copy.
Do not run updates, external searches, or optional cloud localization without approval.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates short design-led motion graphics such as animated text, charts, maps, logo reveals, and overlays.

faq.question: How long should a video be?
faq.answer: Most outputs are under ten seconds. The skill is designed for clips up to about 30 seconds.

faq.question: Can I provide my own logo or image?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide approved assets and describe how they should appear in the animation.

faq.question: Can it make an animated chart?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create bar, line, pie, race, percentage, and statistic-focused animations.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: Some workflows may use search providers, map tiles, or optional image localization. Review and approve those actions first.

faq.question: When should I use another video workflow?
faq.answer: Use a general video workflow for narration, live-action subjects, or longer multi-scene productions.
